headline: Police SI helped convict 'Picchi Raja' escape by unlocking prison van
summary: An SI and a driver were arrested after it was revealed that the convict did not escape on his own, but was helped by the police officers themselves.
details: A Sub-Inspector (SI) of police, Prabir Kumar, allegedly helped convict 'Picchi Raja' escape from a prison van on September 27, by unlocking the van and allowing him to enter a waiting private car.
caption:
A police officer unlocked the prison van and let a convict escape in a private car, then staged a fake escape story.

A Sub-Inspector (SI) of police, Prabir Kumar, allegedly helped convict 'Picchi Raja' escape from a prison van on September 27, by unlocking the van and allowing him to enter a waiting private car.

#Bangladesh #CrimeNews #PoliceCorruption #Justice #Dhaka

Source: Jamuna TV

headline: Prosecution seeks death penalty for Hasanul Haq Inu
summary: The prosecution has appealed to the Supreme Court to increase the 10-year sentence handed down by the International Crimes Tribunal-2.
details: The prosecution has filed an appeal to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court seeking the death penalty for former information minister Hasanul Haq Inu.
This appeal challenges the 10-year imprisonment sentence previously handed down to him by the International Crimes Tribunal-2.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim stated that the 10-year sentence was inadequate given the gravity of the offences and the scale of the attacks.
The appeal includes 11 grounds and seeks the maximum punishment under the law, as well as challenging Inu's acquittal on some charges.
The tribunal observed that Inu communicated with former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and advised on ways to suppress the July uprising, including imposing a curfew and arresting protesters.
Separately, the prosecution has also concluded its arguments seeking the maximum punishment for former Awami League joint general secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif and three others.
caption:
From 10 years to the gallows: Prosecution seeks the death penalty for former minister Hasanul Haq Inu.

The prosecution has filed an appeal to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court seeking the death penalty for former information minister Hasanul Haq Inu.

This appeal challenges the 10-year imprisonment sentence previously handed down to him by the International Crimes Tribunal-2.

Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim stated that the 10-year sentence was inadequate given the gravity of the offences and the scale of the attacks.

The appeal includes 11 grounds and seeks the maximum punishment under the law, as well as challenging Inu's acquittal on some charges.

The tribunal observed that Inu communicated with former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and advised on ways to suppress the July uprising, including imposing a curfew and arresting protesters.

Separately, the prosecution has also concluded its arguments seeking the maximum punishment for former Awami League joint general secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif and three others.
